name: Tute cabrero
description: Tute cabrero is a point-trick elimination game for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. Each deal you aim either to take no tricks or to finish with the highest or lowest point total; middle totals lose. Four losses eliminate a player; the last one or two remaining win. Uses the standard 40-card Spanish deck with follow-suit and optional singing (declaring king-horse for 20 or 40 points after winning a trick).

history.origins: Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the most popular card games there. Tute cabrero is an individual-play variant for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and marriage-style point-trick structure as partnership Tute but with elimination (four losses) and a first-hand rule that coins are trumps and the holder of the two of coins leads. The variant is described in Spanish card-game literature and on dedicated Tute Cabrero pages.
timeline: 20th century: Tute cabrero variant documented as popular in Argentina and Uruguay.

setup.players: Three to six players, each playing for themselves.
setup.dealing: Counter-clockwise; 8 each (5–6p), 10 each (4p), or 13 each plus one to centre (3p). First hand coins are trumps; later hands last card to mano turned for trump.

rules.objective: Avoid being a loser each deal: either take no tricks, or have the highest or lowest point total among those who took tricks. Losers are the middle point totals. A player who loses four times is eliminated; the last one or two players win.
rules.gameplay: Deal and play are counter-clockwise. Deal size varies: 6 players dealer gives 8 each to the other five (dealer sits out); 5 players 8 each; 4 players 10 each; 3 players 13 each plus one to centre. First hand coins are trumps and the holder of the two of coins leads (mano). Later hands the last card dealt to mano is turned for trump (or with 3 players a centre card). Follow suit, beat if possible, trump if unable to follow. After winning a trick you may declare one king-horse combination (40 in trumps, 20 in another suit) before leading. At end of play, count points; losers are determined by point-order rules (e.g. with 5 taking tricks the 2nd, 3rd and 4th highest lose).
keyRules: Singing (cantes) optional after winning a trick

scoring.winCondition: Elimination: avoid being a loser each deal (middle point totals lose). Four losses eliminate a player; last one or two players win. Taking no tricks avoids loss unless one player takes all tricks without singing, in which case all others lose.
